workloads.operationUnit: One complete scalar concatenation scenario
workloads.notes: Scalar strings and compound addition, seven retained cells per scenario. Verified untimed; no timing.
workloads.specification: Join scalar operands with strings in both operand orders and through compound assignment. Preserve seven result cells.
For n iterations, update state = (state * 17 + 13) % 1009. Add state when even and greater than 100; otherwise subtract 1. Start state and checksum at seed.
workloads.notes: Positive bounded integers; every intermediate and checksum remains exactly representable as i64 and JavaScript Number. No overflow, negative remainder, or integer division cases.

workloads.specification: Alternate ASCII padded names according to (i + seed) parity. Trim and lowercase each and append to output array. Return all n results; harness validates their content outside the timed interval.
workloads.notes: ASCII only. Rust owns UTF-8 strings; JavaScript strings are immutable and engine-managed. This measures equivalent transformation results, not equivalent allocation counts or general Unicode semantics.

workloads.specification: Create counter {value:seed, active:true}; call increment once per iteration, alternating active by even value. Sum active values.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Each iteration builds nested record with two scores, clones all mutable storage, modifies original score, and sums original and cloned scores plus cloned score count.
workloads.notes: Explicit shape-specific deep copy preserves independence of all mutable records/arrays. Both runtimes may share immutable string bytes; mutable records and arrays are copied independently; no allocation parity claim. This is not structuredClone performance. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Per iteration push 32 integers seed+i+j, replace element 3 by i, clone vector, sum clone by for-of with continue at seed and break above 20000; toggle a boolean array element and add 1 when true.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Build two string records and a string array per iteration, push a third entry, replace second record score, traverse records adding score+1, clone one indexed record and add score; add string-array length.
workloads.notes: Record copies preserve independent mutable fields; immutable JS strings may share storage. Arrays contain owned native strings/inline records versus JS references. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Build two rows [i,seed] and [seed,i+1]; append i+2 to second row, update first cell to i+3; deep clone; update original; sum cloned rows.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Build catalog with record array and nested rows; push user and score through named helper; iterate fields and nested scores; replace nested profile and read replacement.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Detach nested array and string fields, read sibling score, restore both fields, then sum detached array, restored array first cell, and restored whole-record score. String contents are not part of this numeric checksum.
workloads.notes: Only detached values, untouched sibling, and restored fields are observed. JS assignment aliases storage until replacement; native moves prevent aliases statically. This measures equivalent value flow, not ownership checking cost. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Create local closure each iteration; nested closure increments captured state by 2; outer returns state + seed. Sum returns.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Create escaping counter seeded from seed; call n times; sum incremented values.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: For each i, forward scalar callback taking i and true, plus a single-use callback returning seed. Sum both results.
workloads.notes: JS function is called once by convention; TypeScript does not enforce the source once contract. Same scalar inputs/call counts and results.

workloads.specification: Create counter, move callback through identity and retaining wrapper, invoke twice; then consume a record via a single-use callback returning the entire record and add its seed-valued numeric field.
workloads.notes: JS callable references are not ownership transfers; no moved reference is reused. Same call graph, environment state, and record value flow. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Per iteration create counter, invoke once, replace from same factory with seed, move to new binding and invoke once; sum both results.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Build tree {value:i, children:[{value:seed,children:[]},{value:i+1,children:[]}]}, recursively sum; also mutually recurse depth 8 adding depth values and seed.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Per iteration recurse depth 8 with reusable callback adding seed to depth. Then forward an owned counter through recursive countdown depth 4, invoking at each level. Sum results.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Per iteration recursively construct counter at depth 8, invoke twice, then invoke lazy recursive closure chain depth 4 returning seed.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Build 32 integer elements seed+i+j; remove index 3, then last, then first; sum removed values and all survivors weighted by their one-based position. Also remove a record and a nested row and read their values.
workloads.notes: Same ordered removal contract and valid indices. JS splice returns a newly allocated array; native Vec.remove returns the element. This is an API-contract comparison, not identical algorithm/allocation work. No bounds-error speed ratio.

workloads.specification: Create record {name:Pat,value:i}; call reusable read callback twice, mutate callback once adding seed, then consume callback once returning the record; sum reads and updated values before and after return.
workloads.notes: Same values, callback call counts, and visible state. JavaScript does not enforce ownership/borrow/once restrictions. Immutable string storage and allocation may differ. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Create escaping record environment {name:Pat,value:i}. Each call saves old value, replaces captured record with Sam and value+seed, returns old plus new plus 1. Invoke twice. Also invoke consuming record capture once returning seed.
workloads.notes: Same values, callback call counts, and visible state. JavaScript does not enforce ownership/borrow/once restrictions. Immutable string storage and allocation may differ. String payloads are carried but their contents are not observed by this numeric checksum; optimizers may eliminate unobservable work. Use ascii_strings for measured and content-validated string transformation.

workloads.specification: Grow and retain n integers. Every element contributes to an ordered checksum after timing; output allocation cannot disappear into a numeric-only result.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; all output elements are observed. Allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Build and retain n rows with widths cycling through 0..64. Check every cell and row boundary after timing; exercise inline, spill, and growth thresholds.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; all output elements are observed. Allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Vary widths 0..64, clone, mutate original, remove pseudorandom positions down to half size, append, and checksum both arrays. Exercise repeated shifts and clone independence.
workloads.notes: Integer division is floored only for positive widths; TS uses Math.floor. Native remove versus JS splice result allocation remains an API-contract difference.

workloads.specification: Vary 0..16 wide records containing owned integer rows, deep clone, mutate an original row, remove one cloned record, and observe every numeric field. Record-array inline eligibility is deliberately exceeded.
workloads.notes: Name payload is incidental; numeric fields and nested mutable storage are observed. Shape-specific TS copy preserves independent mutable rows.

workloads.specification: Select from 256 distinct padded mixed-case literals and normalize n results. Observe every output byte; exercise many distinct inputs rather than only two labels.
workloads.notes: Equivalent observable results; all output elements are observed. Allocation and optimization strategies may differ.

workloads.specification: Read externally supplied owned input, trim and lowercase n times, and retain every result. Input creation, validation, and disposal occur outside timing.
workloads.notes: External argv input bypasses static literal normalization. ASCII transform semantics match; outputs are checked byte by byte through the ordered digest.
workloads.inputText: Mixed CASE String 0123456789 ABC xyz AB CD EF

workloads.specification: Build recursive records with root fanout cycling 0..32, grow children, remove a middle child, and recursively traverse survivors. Observe all values.
workloads.notes: Recursive layouts retain heap indirection. Exact tree values and traversal/removal contract match, without cross-runtime allocation parity.

workloads.specification: Clone externally supplied immutable input n times and retain all values; validate every byte after timing. Input creation and output disposal occur outside timing.
workloads.notes: Source strings expose no mutable bytes. JS clones the immutable value by assignment; native may share immutable bytes while preserving independent values.

workloads.specification: Build a forest with fanout 0..4 and additional chain depth 0..3, deep clone, mutate original roots and first children, then retain ordered numeric projections of both copies. Every node and row boundary is checked.
workloads.notes: Independent mutable records and child arrays in both implementations. Native automatic cloning and cleanup are iterative for deep components; the bounded TS copy is recursive. No deep JS stack-limit throughput claim.

workloads.specification: Build a 129-element int array once per batch. For n queries, use fromIndex = (i * 13 + seed) % 387 - 193, covering both directions, clamping, and beyond-end starts. Values are (position * 37 + seed) % 101, including duplicates; needle is (i * 17 + seed) % 137, including misses. Add one for each includes hit. Start checksum at seed.
workloads.notes: Dense homogeneous arrays, typed integer offsets, valid Unicode strings, and bounded exact arithmetic. Receiver construction is timed; external input construction and checksum checking are excluded. No coercion, sparse arrays, floating-point NaN, or owned object identity is compared.

workloads.specification: Build 129 strings from external runtime input once per batch. Most cells trim and lowercase Unicode input; positions with (j * 37 + seed) % 101 == 100 only trim it. Query includes with needle selected by (i + seed) % 3 from lowercase match, mixed-case rare match, or same-length Unicode miss. External input creation and checksum checking are excluded. Content equality is exact, without Unicode normalization.

workloads.specification: Alternate external input and Rust-White_Space-trimmed input; hash their UTF8 byte lengths once per iteration.
workloads.notes: Rust length is standard str.len O1; Unicode TS counterpart explicitly encodes UTF8. This representation/encoding cost is disclosed; it is not ordinary JavaScript UTF16 length. Input creation occurs outside timing; normalization is inside workload setup.

workloads.specification: Slice runtime ASCII input with changing signed start/end bounds; retain all n results.
workloads.notes: ASCII byte/scalar/UTF16 coordinates coincide, so Node ordinary slice matches checked Rust byte slicing. Ordered output checksum and disposal are outside timing.

workloads.specification: Prepare cumulative UTF-8 boundaries using complete scalar charAt results, then retain one byte slice per iteration with signed endpoints selected from those boundaries. Include negative, clamped, equal and reversed ranges; every nonempty endpoint is valid.
workloads.notes: All measured nonempty endpoints are valid UTF-8 boundaries; reversed/equal ranges return empty. Boundary preparation inside workload setup is part of each batch. Node uses explicit UTF8 encoding/decoding; invalid-boundary rejection is covered separately by correctness tests. No UTF-16 partial-unit behavior is claimed.

workloads.specification: Retain one full scalar charAt result per iteration from external input (17 UTF-8 bytes; 9 Unicode scalars). Query (i * 13 + seed) % (coordinates * 2 + 3) - coordinates; out-of-range results are empty.
workloads.notes: One real scalar charAt and result append per iteration; independent ordered codepoint hashing outside timer. Query coordinate width is prepared outside timing where required. Long/middle workloads use 128 iterations because standard chars().nth is linear; small timer differences require caution. No UTF-16 halves/cache/O1 Unicode indexing claim.

workloads.specification: Retain n partial slices of a 3088-byte external UTF8 input. start=(i+seed)%8; end=inputByteLength-1-(i*7+seed)%8. Eight ASCII bytes at each edge guarantee checked boundaries. Every result has3073–3087bytes; no charAt.
workloads.notes: Rust standard Cow slice construction/copy and array growth are timed. Unicode/ASCII inputs match UTF8 byte widths, not scalar or UTF-16 widths. Unicode TS counterpart explicitly encodes and decodes UTF8; ASCII counterpart can use ordinary slice. Input construction and full codepoint hashing stay outside timers. This new contract must not be compared to historical UTF16 operations.

workloads.specification: For n iterations, perform one === and one !== exact string-content comparison across seven strings: empty, ASCII, NUL, composed/decomposed Unicode, astral and external input. Add 1 for equality and 2 for inequality; initial checksum is seed.
workloads.notes: Throughput counts workload loop iterations, each containing two comparisons. Native UTF-8 equality and JavaScript UTF-16 equality agree for valid Unicode content. No Unicode normalization is performed. Array setup and input copies required by Rust ownership occur inside both workload bodies; CLI input construction is outside timing. Independent numeric scalar sequences validate equality, unequal encodings and external equal/missing inputs. Bounded n0–1000000 and seeds0–100.

workloads.specification: For n iterations, perform <, <=, > and >= comparisons across seven ASCII strings: empty, a, aa, alpha, alphabet, z and external input. Add weights 1/2/4/8 for true comparisons; initial checksum is seed.
workloads.notes: Throughput counts workload loop iterations, each containing four comparisons. ASCII UTF-8 bytes and UTF-16 units have matching lexicographic order. workloads.operationUnit: complete reverse-search iteration including needle and position selection and retaining byte index + 1; setup runs once per workload invocation
workloads.specification: Find the greatest ascii substring match start at or before the default byte length. Retain every byte index as index + 1, including misses. Empty needles return the selected position; overlapping matches remain visible.
workloads.notes: Needle pool setup, reverse search, selection and complete result retention are timed. ASCII byte offsets equal UTF16 offsets, so the TypeScript counterpart directly calls actual String.lastIndexOf with the same position pool and no coordinate bridge. Complete observation runs outside timing. These are complete iterations, not isolated-call latency or allocation-parity measurements.

workloads.operationUnit: complete directional-trimming iteration including runtime receiver selection, one trim call and retaining its complete string result; receiver pool setup runs once per invocation
workloads.specification: Use actual trimStart over eight ascii receiver variants constructed with input clones, one-, two- and three-copy repetition, and literals selected by runtime iteration and seed. Preserve the opposite edge and interior contents, retaining every result in order. The timed whitespace domain is shared by pinned Rust and JavaScript; U+0085 and U+FEFF are excluded.
workloads.notes: Receiver pool setup, runtime selection, trimming and complete output retention are timed; full content observation runs outside timing. Pool setup explicitly clones runtime input twice and constructs one-, two- and three-copy owned repetitions, alongside empty, whitespace-only and padded payload literals. Repeated input preserves interior whitespace. Native Cow literals can retain borrowed static trim slices; owned receivers produce independent owned results. JavaScript may reuse immutable string storage. No isolated-call latency or allocation-parity claim.

workloads.operationUnit: One complete Object.is scenario iteration

workloads.operationUnit: One complete Math.f16round scenario iteration

No allocation equivalence claim. Untimed validation is separate from milestone measurements.

workloads.operationUnit: One complete Math.random scenario iteration

No allocation equivalence claim. Untimed validation is separate from milestone measurements.

workloads.operationUnit: One complete string from codes scenario iteration

No allocation equivalence claim. Untimed validation is separate from milestone measurements.

workloads.operationUnit: twenty-two successful positive and negated assertions through stored expectations or Node strict assertions
workloads.specification: Cycle through null, undefined, zero, NaN, negative zero and seven. Verify nullish state, truthiness and NaN state or SameValue identity, then observe active values in a bounded checksum. Verify complementary negated nullish, truthiness and NaN or identity conditions using the same stored expectation. Verify typeof category and negated string category. Check all four numeric relations and their negations using the dynamically selected numeric category index. Verify proximity at default precision and negated proximity at explicit precision 5. Check UTF-16 string length and its negation for a supplementary-plane emoji or repeated ASCII selected by category. Check the active numeric alternative of a union-typed record length property.

Whole workload includes expectation construction, predicate captures, tagged union dispatch, assertions and observation. No timing protocol or sample count changes. Numeric relation checks include a second numeric expectation setup; this remains a whole assertion pipeline comparison. Length checks include string construction and a third native expectation setup. Record length checks include record setup and a fourth native expectation.
